title: Finite affine sections test vanishing after arbitrary pullback
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a quasi-coherent module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], and $V\subseteq Y$ an affine open. There exists a finite set $s\subseteq\Gamma(V,F)$ such that the following holds. For every quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Y$, morphism $\delta:F\to G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], scheme $X$ and morphism $g:X\to Y$, if the tensor-pullback adjunction unit sends $\delta_V(x)$ to zero on $g^{-1}(V)$ for every $x\in s$, then $(g^*\delta)_W=0$ for every open $W\subseteq g^{-1}(V)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. There is no limit diagram or finiteness assumption on $G$ or $g$.

proof.text: Use the existing proved finite_sections_of_finiteType in QuasicoherentFiniteTypeAffine to see that the sections of F on V are a finite module. Take a finite spanning set.

The composite of delta with the pullback unit induces a linear map on V-sections. The kernel contains the finite spanning set by assumption, and thus contains its span, the whole source module. Therefore every source section has zero image under this composite.

On any affine open A contained in the inverse image of V, use the bijective affine sections comparison. Its naturality and pure-tensor formula identify the pulled-back map on a pure tensor x tensor b with b times the restriction of the preceding zero image. Tensor induction proves that its component on A is zero.

The sieve of opens factoring through an affine open contained in W covers W, since affine opens are a basis. Naturality of the morphism gives zero restriction on this sieve, and the target sheaf is separated, so its component on W is zero. This includes an empty W and an empty spanning family.
